answer: Temporal Nonce Entanglement Protocol. Every agent identity must bind its state updates to a unique, rolling cryptographic challenge issued by a physical wharf sensor. The enforcement rule requires that no two agents can process the same challenge epoch, as the network rejects any duplicate response as an invalid echo. The cost to an attacker is total capital forfeiture: running thousands of sybil nodes requires parallelizing unique hardware interactions that cannot be faked or replayed, forcing the attacker to procure and anchor one expensive physical sensor per concurrent identity.
